system_overview: This specification models the voucher issuance operation from RFC 3506, implemented using the Two-Phase Commit protocol. A Voucher Transaction Provider coordinates voucher holders and voucher issuers to atomically issue vouchers, ensuring that all parties either agree to the issuance or the transaction is aborted.
actors_and_components: Four types of participants interact: (1) A Voucher Transaction Provider (the coordinator) that manages the commit/abort decision. (2) Voucher Holders who will receive the issued vouchers. (3) Voucher Issuers who create the vouchers. (4) The vouchers themselves, which transition from a pre-issuance state to a valid state. Communication occurs through a shared message pool; messages are never removed, allowing multiple receipt.
state_variables: The system tracks seven pieces of state: (1) each voucher's current status (pre-issuance or valid), (2) each voucher's lifecycle phase (initial or working), (3) each holder's participation state (waiting, prepared, holding, or aborted), (4) each issuer's participation state (waiting, prepared, issued, or aborted), (5) the coordinator's state (initial or done), (6) the set of participants from which the coordinator has received preparation confirmations, and (7) the pool of all messages sent so far.
initial_state: All vouchers are in the pre-issuance state with lifecycle in the initial phase. All holders and issuers are in the waiting state. The coordinator is in the initial state with an empty set of preparation confirmations and an empty message pool.
actions: The coordinator can: receive preparation confirmations from a holder and an issuer (adding them to its confirmed set), issue a voucher (transitioning it to valid and the lifecycle to working, enabled only when all participants have confirmed preparation), or spontaneously abort (broadcasting an abort message). Each holder can: prepare (sending a preparation confirmation message), spontaneously choose to abort, receive an issuance message (transitioning to the holding state), or receive an abort message (transitioning to the aborted state). Each issuer can: prepare (sending a preparation confirmation), spontaneously choose to abort, receive an issuance message (transitioning to the issued state), or receive an abort message.
safety_properties: Type correctness ensures all variables remain in expected domains. A consistency invariant ensures that no holder and issuer reach conflicting decisions: it must never be the case that a holder is in the holding state while an issuer is aborted, or that a holder is aborted while an issuer is in the issued state. The specification also claims to implement the voucher lifecycle specification as a refinement.
model_bounds: The model-checking configuration uses three vouchers, three holders, and three issuers. Deadlock checking is disabled.
additional_assumptions: Messages are modeled as a set that only grows (messages are never consumed). This simplification allows any message to be received multiple times, which does not cause problems in this protocol. Preparation messages from the coordinator to participants are not explicitly modeled; participants spontaneously decide to prepare. Abort messages from participants to the coordinator are also eliminated; instead, the coordinator can spontaneously decide to abort.
